import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

def clahe(gray, tiles=(8,8), clip=2.5):
    h,w=gray.shape
    ty,tx=tiles
    th,tw=h//ty,w//tx
    out=np.zeros_like(gray,dtype=float)
    cdfs=[]
    for i in range(ty):
        for j in range(tx):
            t=gray[i*th:(i+1)*th, j*tw:(j+1)*tw]
            hist,_=np.histogram(t,bins=256,range=(0,256))
            hist=hist.astype(float)
            limit=clip*hist.mean()
            excess=np.sum(np.maximum(hist-limit,0))
            hist=np.minimum(hist,limit)+excess/256
            cdf=np.cumsum(hist); cdf/=cdf[-1]
            cdfs.append(cdf)
    # simple: apply per-tile with bilinear interpolation approx (nearest for simplicity)
    for i in range(ty):
        for j in range(tx):
            cdf=cdfs[i*tx+j]
            t=gray[i*th:(i+1)*th, j*tw:(j+1)*tw]
            out[i*th:(i+1)*th, j*tw:(j+1)*tw]=cdf[t]*255
    return out.astype(np.uint8)

im=np.array(Image.open('radiograph.jpg').convert('L'))
r=clahe(im,tiles=(10,16),clip=2.0)
Image.fromarray(r).save('/tmp/clahe.png')
print('ok')
EOF
